focus: Legacy archive and platform decommissioning: extracting closed history into self-describing open-format archives, vendor exit and decommissioning terms, records retention periods, data meaning preservation, dual systems of record risk, legal retention requirements
rationale: This document extends the Halyard cutover programme into post-cutover decommissioning — what happens to the closed history when the vendor platform is switched off after the last site goes live. I expanded CutoverStrategy as the hub to place the new decommissioning decisions under, and Narrative_SingleSourceOfTruthUntilFinalCutover because the document directly continues that narrative (vendor as system of record until last site live → platform switch-off → archive extraction). Narrative_ContainedPainOverUnboundedRisk is included because Xavier's argument (contained extraction effort now vs. unbounded decay risk of an unpatched orphan system) and Tanya's dual-systems-of-record argument both echo the contained-pain-over-unbounded-risk framing. Position_ReferenceDataSourceOfRecordTransition is included as the complementary position — it covers what data transfers to internal systems, while this document covers what stays behind in the archive. Position_SiteCutoverSequencingStrategy provides the sequencing context that determines when 'last site goes live' triggers decommissioning. All three actor nodes are included for correct attribution. I deliberately did NOT expand Narrative_StrictWorkloadIsolationDuringCutover, Position_CutoverReportingReadIsolation, Position_PostGoLiveSoakDurationBasis, or Position_CrossSiteOperationalLearning because this document does not touch reporting isolation, soak durations, or cross-site learning — including them would be reaching beyond the document's scope.
